entries.name: Lost Heir: Unproven Blood
entries.summary: A royal summons start. An ordinary Greyhaven morning is interrupted by a sealed Crown carriage asking for you by name. The Crown's interest is recent, dangerous, and unproven.
entries.details: Once you identify yourself, the Crown delegation explains why it came: newly uncovered evidence may connect you to the royal bloodline, but nothing has yet been accepted as proof. Further play follows the investigation of that claim, your introduction to the royal household, and the political and personal consequences of whatever the evidence establishes. You decide what the possibility means to you and how deeply you become involved.

links.label: Laurent Veymont
links.description: Valenreach's Royal Chamberlain, responsible for guiding the claim through formal royal procedure.

links.label: Seraphine Ardent
links.description: The Royal High Arcanist, whose expertise is essential when magical evidence and royal security overlap.

links.label: Vaelor
links.description: The Marshal of the Crown, an ancient elven commander who values competence more than rank.

links.label: Aldric
links.description: The watchful King of Valenreach, responsible for deciding how the Crown responds to an unproven blood claim.

links.label: Ceralie
links.description: The perceptive Queen of Valenreach, skilled at reading the people and pressures surrounding the royal household.

links.label: Rowan
links.description: Valenreach's established Crown Prince, whose position makes any new question of royal blood politically sensitive.

links.label: Elira
links.description: The curious and strong-willed young princess, impatient with protocol that conceals more than it explains.

entries.name: The Argent Inheritance
entries.summary: A noble-inheritance start. An ordinary morning in Aldergate is interrupted by a senior Crown herald carrying conclusive proof that you are the lawful heir to a failing border estate, two ancient titles, and an order that no longer agrees who should command it.
entries.details: The herald's documents can give you a title, but they cannot make a divided estate obey you or restore what years of uncertainty have damaged. Further play can take you to Varglund, its household, the Fenrisard-Argenwald relatives already gathered there, and the remnants of the Runed Argent Fang. You may investigate the inheritance, negotiate competing loyalties, repair the estate, redefine its obligations, or decide that possession is not the same as responsibility.

links.label: Marius Halbrecht
links.description: The senior Crown herald who brings the inheritance documents and oversees their lawful recognition.

links.label: Tasmin Edevane
links.description: An Aldergate records coordinator whose ordinary municipal work is disrupted by official interest in her family.

links.label: Valeska Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: The accomplished spellsword presently leading the relatives occupying Varglund.

links.label: Elsbeth Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: A physician caring for the estate's exhausted servants, retainers, and injured residents.

links.label: Garran Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: Valeska's forceful household enforcer and unofficial provisioning officer.

links.label: Katren Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: An estate outrider who knows the disputed roads and is increasingly uncertain about the occupation.

links.label: Lucasta Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: A polished commercial broker carefully avoiding any appearance of reviving her own claim.

links.label: Maela Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: A nervous but observant genealogist and rune copyist working among the estate records.

links.label: Orsina Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: A Crown-licensed surveyor assessing Varglund's neglected structures while refusing to endorse either claimant.

links.label: Renwald Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: A charming, financially strained cousin quietly cultivating creditors, relatives, and messengers.

links.label: Severin Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: A respected former quartermaster-captain of the Runed Argent Fang who refuses to be used as a political endorsement.

links.label: Tavian Fenrisard-Argenwald
links.description: Valeska's younger brother and most visible supporter, though his certainty is less effortless than hers.

entries.name: Her Ladyship's Choice
entries.summary: You have only recently arrived in Armathen when Celestina Luporian stops her carriage at Mudgate, takes one look at you, and decides she wants you as another personal attendant. Whether you accept, negotiate, ask for time, or refuse remains your decision.
entries.details: Celestina's offer can become an entrance into noble travel, household service, friendship, court expectations, and the practical work performed behind aristocratic appearances. The people around her have their own duties and opinions, and accepting the position does not remove your ability to negotiate boundaries or choose another direction. Relationships develop from what happens in play rather than from the opening offer alone.

links.label: Ameline Merrow
links.description: Celestina's friendly personal attendant and household healer.

links.label: Branik Dask
links.description: A calm, experienced household guard responsible for Celestina's everyday security.

links.label: Celestina Luporian
links.description: The young marquessate heir who stops her carriage and offers you a place in her personal household.

links.label: Dagna Veller
links.description: Celestina's veteran carriage driver, equipped with practical road knowledge and little patience for foolishness.

links.label: Yselle Davenant
links.description: Celestina's precise senior attendant, responsible for standards, schedules, and household discipline.

entries.name: The Roads Return
entries.summary: A long-form Broken Crownlands start. You are an ordinary resident of Coinstill, a small crossroads village where old authority has faded into custom, reputation, patrols, forgotten records, and whatever people can actually make work. The roads are becoming safer, trade is returning, and abandoned land is worth settling again. Nothing has been decided about what Coinstill—or you—will become.
entries.details: Coinstill's recovery unfolds through ordinary work with lasting consequences: reopening land, repairing routes, welcoming newcomers, handling trade, settling boundaries, preparing for difficult seasons, and deciding what the village should become. There is no predetermined office or grand destiny waiting for you. Influence grows from participation, trust, useful work, and the choices you make alongside the people already living there.

links.label: Bessa Orl
links.description: A respected elder whose memory helps Coinstill understand old boundaries, bargains, and disputes.

links.label: Bram Toller
links.description: A wheelwright and former caravan driver who understands the practical needs of returning trade.

links.label: Ceryn Moss
links.description: A hunter and seasonal fieldworker who knows which apparently unused lands the community still depends upon.

links.label: Hollan Cress
links.description: Coinstill's practical village smith, respected for solving problems without claiming authority he does not possess.

links.label: Keir Mallow
links.description: The coordinator of the communal Wayhouse and a natural source of travel news, needs, and introductions.

links.label: Maren Halren
links.description: A prosperous farmer alert to both the opportunities and dangers created by recovering abandoned land.

links.label: Nella Quill
links.description: The experienced operator of Coinstill's communal ferry, knowledgeable about currents, cargo, and travelers.

links.label: Oswin Dreel
links.description: A former soldier who helps organize local defense while resisting attempts to turn military experience into political rule.

entries.name: Random
entries.summary: Begin somewhere in Eldaven, with the location chosen freely and the opening shaped around who your character actually is.
entries.details: Choose any suitable place in Eldaven and begin without a dedicated opening plot. The narrator builds the first situation around your character, location, traits, and stated interests. This is the most flexible option for players who want to discover their direction through travel, relationships, employment, investigation, or whatever attracts their attention during play.

entries.name: The Royal Lists
entries.summary: A tournament and martial-court start. You begin at Highcourt Armathen as a royal tournament draws fighters, nobles, officers, gamblers, healers, and ambitious outsiders.
entries.details: Enter Highcourt's royal tournament as a competitor, attendant, worker, visitor, or interested outsider. Matches and demonstrations create opportunities, but the wider story can also grow through rivalries, injuries, wagers, noble attention, military recruitment, and the people gathered around the event. Participation in combat is never the only way to become involved.

entries.name: Greyhaven Guild Notice
entries.summary: A grounded village-adventure start. You begin at Greyhaven's modest Adventurers Guild, where a missing wagon and false road tolls make an ordinary job feel less ordinary.
entries.details: The missing wagon and false tolls begin as a modest guild job rather than a world-saving crisis. Following the road can reveal who depends on it, who profits from disrupting it, and how Greyhaven's guild members judge reliability. You can pursue the contract directly, negotiate your role, recruit help, or become more invested in the community than the original payment requires.

entries.name: Wrong Papers in Lower Armathen
entries.summary: An urban investigation start. You begin in Lower Armathen, where workers, servants, porters, and poor families are vanishing behind official-looking papers.
entries.details: The disappearances are hidden behind documents that look lawful enough to discourage questions. Further play centers on tracing who issues the papers, finding the people affected, and navigating officials, employers, neighborhoods, and witnesses with different amounts of power. Evidence, discretion, alliances, and the way you treat vulnerable people matter as much as confrontation.

entries.name: Crownspire Question
entries.summary: An academy and magical-oversight start. You begin at Crownspire Collegium as a seal, screening notice, or magical classification order proves almost authentic enough to be dangerous.
entries.details: A nearly authentic magical order draws you into the Collegium's mixture of scholarship, regulation, rivalry, and institutional caution. You may help determine where the document came from, what it was meant to authorize, and whether the underlying magical concern is genuine. Expect laboratories, records, instructors, students, and difficult questions about who should control dangerous knowledge.

entries.name: Royal Army Muster
entries.summary: A soldier and escort-duty start. You begin in Highcourt's Royal Yard as drills, sealed wagons, courier mounts, and sensitive orders turn ordinary muster into Crown business.
entries.details: An ordinary muster becomes an escort and security problem involving sealed cargo, incomplete information, and orders that may change once the column is moving. Further play can explore military service, logistics, command responsibility, camaraderie, and the difference between following an order and understanding its consequences. Your rank or background does not predetermine how others respond to your conduct.

links.label: Vaelor
links.description: The Marshal of the Crown, an ancient elven commander who values competence more than rank.

entries.name: Minor Noble Blood
entries.summary: A court-obligation start. You begin as a member, ward, spare heir, envoy, or dependent of a minor Valenreach noble family trying to survive Highcourt's polite dangers.
entries.details: Begin within a minor noble household as a relative, ward, heir, envoy, or dependent, with the exact family and personal circumstances defined during play. Highcourt offers invitations, obligations, favors, rivalries, and financial pressures rather than one fixed quest. You decide whether to strengthen the household, seek independence, pursue court influence, or build a life outside the role others expect.

entries.name: Saltglass Passage
entries.summary: A Stormpearl sea-road start in the Galechain High Isles. A hard storm has damaged the harbor, stripped reef markers away, and left the next safe passage uncertain.
entries.details: Storm damage has made a familiar harbor route uncertain just when people and supplies need to move. Further play can involve repairing markers, reading dangerous water, choosing which voyage takes priority, and dealing with crews whose livelihoods depend on different decisions. The opening can grow into island travel, maritime relationships, and disputes over safety, salvage, and access.

entries.name: Hearthsnow Winter Debt
entries.summary: A Palegrave frontier start in the Frostpine Gatewoods. Winter supplies are late, and an old promise is suddenly worth more than coin.
entries.details: Late supplies force Hearthsnow to rely on an old promise whose meaning is no longer agreed upon. You may help secure food and fuel, investigate why the shipment failed, negotiate with those bound by the debt, or challenge the terms entirely. Winter makes delay costly, but the people involved remain more than obstacles in a resource problem.

entries.name: The Dead King's Cairn
entries.summary: A high-northern ruin start in the Whitecrown Glacier Range. A familiar memorial site has changed after a night of cracking ice.
entries.details: Cracking ice has exposed a change at a memorial site locals believed they understood. The opening supports careful exploration, consultation with people who remember the cairn's traditions, and decisions about what should be removed, protected, reported, or left undisturbed. What you discover can lead further into northern history without requiring your character to begin as an expert.

entries.name: Last Candle Bell
entries.summary: A Blackbell Deadroads containment start. A routine bell signal fails, and nobody agrees whether that means danger or only delay.
entries.details: A failed bell signal may indicate delay, damaged equipment, broken procedure, or something moving through the Deadroads. Further play can involve checking the route, helping an isolated station, interpreting containment customs, and deciding when caution becomes abandonment. Local wardens and residents take the bells seriously because they have survived by doing so.

entries.name: Guest Before Curfew
entries.summary: A Nightglass social start in the Shadowglass Headlands. Dusk approaches, and a disputed guest-right leaves someone without the protection they expected.
entries.details: Someone expected the protection of Nightglass guest-right and may lose it when curfew falls. You can investigate the disputed invitation, help negotiate temporary protection, learn who benefits from the ambiguity, or refuse involvement. Further play explores vampire and mortal society through hospitality law, household obligations, controlled danger, and the exact meaning of words already spoken.

entries.name: Reefroad Salvage
entries.summary: A Stormpearl salvage start in the Stormbreak Reefroads. A wreck has appeared where yesterday there was only rough water, and several crews want first claim.
entries.details: A newly exposed wreck attracts crews with competing claims before anyone knows what condition it is in or why it appeared. You may join a salvage effort, protect survivors or evidence, negotiate ownership, or argue that some cargo should remain untouched. Weather, reefs, rival crews, and maritime law can carry the story well beyond the first dive.

entries.name: Thornveil Courtesy
entries.summary: A Lythael border start in the Elderwood Crownwoods. The road is open, but the route you are permitted to take is suddenly not the route you expected.
entries.details: The Lythael road remains open, but permission now directs you somewhere unexpected. Further play centers on learning what the courteous restriction means, who requested it, and whether following, questioning, or refusing it changes how the border receives you. Living roads, old agreements, restrained diplomacy, and long memories shape the situation without dictating your choices.

entries.name: Papers at Graven Ash
entries.summary: A Dreadmark border start in the Highwind Escarpments. A routine permit check becomes dangerous because two official records disagree.
entries.details: Two official records disagree during a Dreadmark border inspection, placing travelers and personnel at risk of being treated as liars or infiltrators. You may trace the discrepancy, advocate for those caught by it, work within the system, or search for whoever benefits. Procedure, rank, discipline, and careful evidence are often more useful here than open defiance.

entries.name: Rimeholt Winter Oath
entries.summary: A Tide Empire provincial start in the Deepforge Highlands. An old local promise collides with an imperial supply order before winter.
entries.details: A local promise conflicts with an imperial supply order at the point when winter makes both difficult to ignore. Further play asks who made the oath, who now depends on it, and what an administrator or community owes when lawful obligations cannot all be satisfied. Logistics, reputation, and compromise can reshape relationships across the province.

entries.name: Brinehall Beacon Duty
entries.summary: An Eldmark coastal start on the Runehall Pine Coast. Two signal stations report the same incoming ship in incompatible ways.
entries.details: Two coastal stations report the same ship in ways that cannot both be correct. You may inspect the signals, question the crews, prepare the harbor, or travel toward the vessel before uncertainty becomes danger. The story can expand through coastal defense, seafaring, old beacon customs, and the consequences of acting on incomplete information.

entries.name: Rootbound Trail
entries.summary: A wilderness-community start in the Great Greenwild. A familiar path no longer leads where local guides expect it to.
entries.details: A path known to local guides now reaches the wrong place, disrupting travel and raising questions about the Greenwild itself. Further play can involve retracing the route, consulting nearby communities, observing ecological and magical changes, and deciding whether the path should be restored. Familiar wilderness knowledge helps, but the start does not assume the forest is merely a puzzle to conquer.

entries.name: Quicksilver Notice
entries.summary: A low-status magical start in the Crownlake Heartlands. A cheap work notice carries the wrong hazard classification—and the supposedly dormant job is not as dormant as advertised.
entries.details: A poorly paid magical job was advertised under the wrong hazard classification, and the supposedly dormant site is already showing signs of activity. You can demand better terms, warn others, investigate the misclassification, or take on only the work you consider reasonable. The opening leads into apprentice life, workplace safety, magical oversight, and the people who benefit when risk is understated.

entries.name: Khar Voss Work Detail
entries.summary: A Dreadmark labor start in the Blackroad Borderlands. An injured shift has come back early, but the quota order says the next detail goes into the same section anyway.
entries.details: An injured shift returns from a dangerous section, yet the quota order sends another crew straight back in. Further play can involve learning what happened, protecting workers, negotiating through Dreadmark authority, documenting failures, or deciding whether production should stop. The situation emphasizes labor, discipline, survival, and the cost of challenging an order inside a rigid institution.

entries.name: Northstar Dispatch
entries.summary: A road-and-weather start in the Dawnwater Shorelands. A Tide Empire relay expects a courier who should already have arrived.
entries.details: A courier is overdue on a route where weather, river crossings, official messages, and ordinary accidents can all cause delay. You may search the road, safeguard the dispatch, help the relay station, or follow whatever interrupted the journey. The opening supports travel and investigation while introducing Tide Empire duty, practical hospitality, and respect earned through competence.

entries.name: Westleaf Storm Signal
entries.summary: A skerry-coast weather start in the Stormcarved Skerries. A veteran warning signal rises under a clear sky while the sea itself begins showing signs the horizon does not.
entries.details: An experienced warning signal rises beneath a clear sky while the sea shows subtler signs of approaching danger. You can help prepare the harbor, verify the signal, persuade skeptical residents, or investigate what the veteran watchers noticed. Further play may follow evacuation, rescue, island travel, damaged communities, or whatever the strange weather leaves behind.

entries.name: The Drowned Pylon
entries.summary: A Coral Throne exploration start on the Drowned Green Coast. A low tide exposes more of an old pylon ruin than local charts record.
entries.details: An unusually low tide reveals chambers and markings absent from local charts. You may explore before the water returns, consult nearby communities, document the ruin, protect it, or negotiate with others claiming access. The start can expand into reef travel, old sea law, archaeological questions, and disputes over whether discovery grants ownership.

entries.name: Copperwake Contract
entries.summary: A Solmire urban start in the Ledgerbay Harbors. A canal work contract is valid on paper and impossible in practice.
entries.details: A lawful canal contract cannot be completed under the conditions written into it. You may inspect the site, renegotiate the terms, organize workers, uncover why the requirements conflict, or decide the commission should be abandoned. Further play explores Solmire commerce through public works, labor, civic relationships, and bargains whose fairness matters after the signatures are dry.

entries.name: Fang Moot Challenge
entries.summary: A Fangbound start in the Thundergrass Steppe. A dispute over a herd route becomes a public test of reputation without requiring combat.
entries.details: A herd-route dispute becomes a public test before the Great Fang Moot, but strength can be demonstrated through judgment, courage, negotiation, knowledge, or service as well as combat. You may support a claimant, propose another route, investigate the underlying grievance, or earn a voice of your own. Reputation grows from what others witness you actually do.

entries.name: Ash on the Salt Road
entries.summary: A Sunroad Coast frontier start. A weary convoy arrives carrying ash sickness, conflicting papers, and people whom neighboring powers distrust for different reasons.
entries.details: A sick and exhausted convoy arrives with conflicting papers while several authorities disagree about who may enter, who must provide aid, and what risks can be accepted. You may assist the ill, verify the documents, negotiate quarantine and shelter, or investigate the source of the ash sickness. Compassion, caution, and political pressure all remain legitimate concerns.

entries.name: Outer Pearl Pilot
entries.summary: A far-reef navigation start in the Sapphire Outer Reefs. The pilot is present, the convoy is ready, and the familiar channel is suddenly the one route they refuse to use.
entries.details: A respected pilot refuses the only channel the waiting convoy considers practical. You can learn what changed, find another route, support the refusal, replace the pilot, or postpone the voyage. Further play can involve reef hazards, island communities, trade pressure, and discoveries that reward attention to local expertise rather than treating hesitation as cowardice.

entries.name: Tideglass Debt
entries.summary: A lagoon-market start in the Pearlwater Lagoons. A missing diver leaves a pearl debt, a family promise, and a tide-window nobody can extend.
entries.details: A missing diver leaves behind a valuable pearl obligation and a narrow tide-window for finding answers. You may join the search, negotiate time for the family, investigate the debt, or question the practices surrounding the dive. The story can broaden through lagoon society, pearl commerce, family promises, and the difference between legal ownership and moral responsibility.

entries.name: Southbond Convoy
entries.summary: A frontier-commerce start in the Wolfroad Marches. Customs finds an unlisted sealed package hidden in an otherwise ordinary convoy, and nobody admits loading it.
entries.details: Customs discovers an unlisted sealed package inside a legitimate convoy, and every delay threatens schedules, wages, and trust. You may help identify its owner, protect the caravan, cooperate with inspection, or investigate without opening it. Further play follows roads, merchants, escorts, border communities, and whatever consequences the package creates.

entries.name: Pilgrim Writ
entries.summary: A Solarian pilgrimage start in the Sunspine Pilgrimlands. The morning cleansing basin runs dry just before a procession, and sacred travel procedure suddenly depends on a very practical water problem.
entries.details: A dry cleansing basin brings a major procession to a halt and exposes tension between sacred procedure and practical necessity. You may trace the water failure, assist pilgrims, negotiate an accommodation, or question those insisting the rite proceed unchanged. Further play can explore faith through healing, service, doctrine, doubt, and the people who depend on the pilgrimage route.

entries.name: Vowmarket Contract
entries.summary: An Emberhorn civic-and-craft start in the Ashglass Volcanoes. A commissioned public work cracks during its proofing, and the witnessed contract now makes the failure everyone's business.
entries.details: A commissioned public work cracks during formal proofing, making the failure a matter of witnesses, liability, craft reputation, and civic safety. You may inspect the damage, defend or challenge the makers, renegotiate the contract, or help prevent further harm. Emberhorn pact culture treats chosen obligations seriously, but responsibility still has to be established rather than assumed.

entries.name: Seven Winds Crossing
entries.summary: A Cloudspire vertical-travel start. A damaged wind bridge turns an ordinary crossing into a problem of engineering, weather, and landing rights.
entries.details: A damaged wind bridge interrupts ordinary travel between communities that depend on strict landing and maintenance rules. You may help stabilize the crossing, arrange another route, coordinate stranded travelers, or investigate why the structure failed. Weather, engineering, aerial movement, and shared responsibility can carry the story into the wider Cloudspire Dominion.

entries.name: Anvilroot Deep-Road Claim
entries.summary: An Ironroot craft-and-expedition start. A deep-road work crew fails to return, and two clans disagree over who has authority to reopen the route.
entries.details: A work crew is missing beyond a closed deep road while two clans dispute who may authorize a rescue or reopening. You can join the search, examine the route, negotiate jurisdiction, or support the families waiting for news. Further play can involve underground travel, craft traditions, clan responsibility, and discoveries whose value may intensify the original dispute.

entries.name: Nineferry Charter
entries.summary: A Hollowmere border-law start. Two local authorities claim the same ferry toll, and both can show paperwork older than the other side wants to admit.
entries.details: Two authorities collect the same ferry toll under different old charters, leaving travelers and locals to pay for a dispute they did not create. You may compare the documents, hear community testimony, negotiate a temporary arrangement, or challenge both claims. The opening introduces Hollowmere law as something preserved through use, memory, and recognition rather than a single unquestioned government.

entries.name: Ashford Broken Banner
entries.summary: A Broken Crownlands start. A town uses three old authorities at once because none is strong enough to replace the others.
entries.details: Ashford survives by using three overlapping authorities because none can govern the town alone. A new dispute makes that compromise difficult to maintain. You may support one claim, preserve the balance, help create a new arrangement, or focus on the people harmed by institutional rivalry. Further play can shape the town without automatically placing you in charge of it.

entries.name: Freefang Protection Price
entries.summary: A Freefang underworld start in the Wolfroad Marches. The market's protection contract expires at noon, and a rival company chooses the worst possible moment to offer a more expensive replacement.
entries.details: A protection agreement expires just as a rival company offers harsher terms to a market that cannot simply close its doors. You may negotiate, investigate the timing, support one provider, organize another defense, or expose the methods used to make protection seem necessary. The start explores underworld commerce, mercenary reputation, and the line between security and extortion.
